small_guidance:
- Add larger-tile autotune configs sized for M=N=K=4096 on Ada (e.g. BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=4 stages=4, BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 stages=3, BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_K=32) and prune the slow ones; current set may be skipping the optimal point.
- Cache `scale_full`/`shift_full` (and `B_t`) across forward calls keyed on bn parameter pointers so the eval path doesn't recompute them every step; also pre-store them as module buffers contiguous on GPU.
- The transposed-weight path (`B_t = W.t().contiguous()`) doubles weight memory and pollutes L2; instead pass `W` directly with swapped strides (`stride_bk=W.stride(1)=1`, `stride_bn=W.stride(0)=K`) so B is loaded as `[K, N]` view of the original row-major weight — saves the contiguous copy and the cache invalidation.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a split-K or stream-K GEMM: with M=N=K=4096 a single-tile-per-output-block kernel under-occupies the 128 SMs of the 4090; stream-K balances tiles and typically beats classic tiling on large square GEMMs.
- Consider an FP16/BF16 tensor-core path: cast inputs to bf16 on the fly (or keep an fp32 accumulator with `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` and ensure inputs are tf32-friendly) — the reference cuBLAS uses TF32, so make sure `allow_tf32=True` is explicitly set in `tl.dot`.
- Restructure forward so the eval-path constants (`scale`, `shift_with_bias`, transposed or stride-swapped weight) are precomputed once at first eval call and stored as buffers; the current per-forward `torch.no_grad()` arithmetic and `.contiguous()` calls add measurable host-side overhead at this batch size.
